decisions.reason: As a valve-related pipeline component very close to the firm's established fittings, processes, and infrastructure customers, it fits existing knowledge well and is more likely to be refined than withdrawn.
The pipe support bracket builds directly on the firm's fabrication and project-customer know-how, so management can interpret market feedback effectively and improve it within the existing range.

Although the public waste bin is more distant from the core pipeline business, it still uses the firm's metalworking and powder-coating capabilities and by now likely benefits from learning gained across the newer public-space product line.

The waste bin with ashtray remains outside the firm's original core, but its several-model line gives more scope to absorb customer feedback and exploit shared fabrication and coating knowledge, supporting retention.

Outdoor public ashtrays are a peripheral diversification, yet they are technologically related to the firm's coated metal products and can be supported by experience gathered from selling to municipal and trade buyers.
